controls.label: Infrared color
controls.qualification: False color from its measured flux in three infrared bands (Rajan et al. (2017), as compiled in Best, Liu, Magnier & Dupuy (2024), The UltracoolSheet v2.1 (Zenodo); zero points from the SVO Filter Profile Service). The disc itself is unresolved; darkening toward the edge from a model atmosphere.
controls.notes: 51 Eridani b's brightness in three infrared bands as one color: red MKO K 2.184 µm, green MKO H 1.614 µm, blue MKO J 1.2417 µm (Rajan et al. (2017), as compiled in Best, Liu, Magnier & Dupuy (2024), The UltracoolSheet v2.1 (Zenodo); zero points from the SVO Filter Profile Service), on a range shared with this planet alone, from zero to its brightest band (mko j), so the color shows its band ratios; brightness is not compared across planets at different distances. Not a natural color; nobody has resolved its disc. The darkening toward the edge is the quadratic law fitted to the MKO H intensity PICASO 4.1 (Batalha et al. 2019, ApJ 878, 70) computes from Exo-REM cloudy (Charnay et al. 2018, ApJ 854, 172; 3.16 times solar metallicity, C/O 0.65) model atmospheres at 632 K and log g 3.7, read between the models YGP_600K_logg3.5, YGP_600K_logg4.0, YGP_650K_logg3.5, YGP_650K_logg4.0 (u1 1.237, u2 -0.291; the law fits each model's eight angles within 0.33% of the centre): a cloudy model, the one Balmer et al. (2025), arXiv:2503.13608 fit to this planet, because no table reaches a planet this cold and nobody has resolved its disc.
